mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates one signed difference to another, translate it directly as (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of terms on both sides.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement of the form 'The number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have.'
mathgap.example: Interpreting the right side as an absolute difference or swapping C and D, e.g., treating (A - B) = |C - D| or (A - B) = (D - C).

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person, set that person's current count to the given number at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any statement like 'X has N oranges' or 'X has N carrots'.
mathgap.example: Assuming the count is unchanged later despite subsequent transfer statements that modify it.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'X has N more items than Y' as X = Y + N, and 'X has N fewer items than Y' as X = Y - N.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement uses 'more' or 'fewer' to compare two quantities.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X has N more than Y' as X = Y - N, reversing the sign.

mathgap.title: Split‑all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says a person splits all their items equally among two recipients, assign each recipient half of the total.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Statements of the form 'X splits all their items equally between Y and Z'.
mathgap.example: Dividing the items unevenly or forgetting to halve the total.

mathgap.title: Targeted constraint extraction for queried variable
mathgap.principle: When the goal is to find a specific person's count, first gather all equations and statements that involve that person, ignoring unrelated constraints.
mathgap.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a problem where a single person's count is queried.
mathgap.example: Including constraints about unrelated people, leading to unnecessary complexity and potential confusion.

mathgap.title: Sequential transfer handling with updated counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately subtract the transferred amount from the giver and add it to the receiver, updating their counts for any subsequent statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement of the form 'X gives N items to Y' is encountered.
mathgap.example: Applying a later transfer before an earlier one, causing counts to be off for statements that depend on the earlier state.

mathgap.title: Substitution of known signed differences into signed difference equalities
mathgap.principle: If a signed difference on one side of an equality is already known from a direct statement or previous inference, substitute its numeric value before solving the remaining equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When solving equations that involve signed differences, and some of those differences have already been determined.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known difference as a symbolic term and failing to substitute its value, leaving the system underdetermined.

mathgap.title: Chronological evaluation of statements
mathgap.principle: Process the statements in the order given, updating counts after each step; later statements refer to the updated counts from earlier steps.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process, especially when transfers or updates appear.
mathgap.example: Using a person's original count in a later statement that should reflect a prior transfer.

mathgap.title: Preserve order in signed difference statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement mentions the 'difference between X and Y', treat it as the signed difference X - Y, preserving the order, not as an absolute difference.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Any occurrence of the phrase 'difference between X and Y' in a statement.
mathgap.example: Swapping X and Y to compute Y - X or taking the absolute value |X - Y|.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences or swapping term order
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model confuses the phrase 'difference between X and Y' with an unsigned magnitude, or mistakenly reverses the order of terms.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always interpret 'difference between X and Y' as the signed expression X - Y, preserving the given order, and never take absolute values.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers out of order or assumes they are independent of statement order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process transfer statements exactly when they appear, updating counts before any later statements that reference those persons.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats a direct count as a permanent value, forgetting that subsequent transfers can change it.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Remember that explicit counts are initial values; apply any later transfers to adjust them before using the final count.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by N times' as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase 'increase by N times' can be read as 'add N' instead of 'multiply by N'.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Interpret 'increase by N times' as a multiplication: new count = old count * N.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model overlooks conditions that may affect whether a transfer occurs, treating all transfers as unconditional.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Read the full context of transfer statements; if a condition is present, ensure the transfer is applied only when the condition holds.
